help.flow.title: How it works
help.flow.body:
1. Record your game (or use clips you already have, e.g. from Medal).
2. Analyze the video with Gemini (best after the game; it also works with Fortnite open).
3. Learn: the report shows timestamped mistakes and good plays, exactly what to search on YouTube / TikTok / Google, your levels go up, and the training plan updates.
Optional: the experimental Live Coach shows short tips top-left while you practice.
help.before.title: Before you play
help.before.body:
• Open the app first. It can stay next to the clock (tray).
• In Fortnite set Display Mode: Windowed Fullscreen (exclusive fullscreen may record black).
• Record: press {toggle} to start and again to stop; the video is loaded for analysis automatically. Live Coach on/off: {live}. A short message top-left confirms each press. (Also: {start} starts what the record card shows, {stop} stops it.)
• Short sessions (2–10 minutes) give the clearest feedback and use less of your free quota.
help.after.title: After the game
help.after.body:
1. Gameplay Analysis → Load this recording (or Choose video…, or open a clip from the Clip library).
2. Pick the game mode, depth (Standard is a good start) and focus skills. For a long match use Start at or Last part of the match to analyze the fights instead of the landing.
3. Analyze with Gemini → check the confirmation (requests, upload size) → Yes. If Fortnite is still open the app asks first; preparation runs at low priority.
4. The report opens in History when it is done. You can keep using the app meanwhile.
help.report.title: Reading the report
help.report.body:
• Every mistake has a timestamp, what you did, what was better, why, a drill, the evidence seen in the video and a confidence %.
• Could not be judged lists what the video did not show; nothing is guessed.
• Scores are AI estimates from this video only; counts (sessions, mistakes, minutes) are measured.
• The same mistake in 2+ sessions becomes a priority on the dashboard and in your training plan.
help.levels.title: Levels & XP
help.levels.body:
• XP comes only from good plays the coach saw: easy 10, medium 25, hard 50 (× the coach's confidence).
• Each skill has a level; the overall level adds them up. Tiers: Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum → Diamond → Master → Legend.
• Mistakes never lower a level. Re-analyzing the same video gives no XP again.
help.faq.title: Problems & answers
help.faq.body:
“This does not look like an API key” — copy the key again from aistudio.google.com/apikey and use the Paste button. The hint under the field shows the length (a Gemini key is usually 39 characters starting with AIza).

Test connection fails — check internet; make sure the key is from Google AI Studio (not Google Cloud with billing); create a new key if needed.

“Free daily quota used up” — wait until tomorrow or lower the analyzed minutes; the app never switches to a paid model.

Recording stops when I switch to Fortnite — Windows briefly cuts off screen capture when Fortnite opens or changes display mode. The app resumes automatically and joins the parts when you click Load. For the most stable recording, start it when Fortnite is already in the lobby.

Recording does not start / black video — use Windowed Fullscreen; run Check hardware; try 1080p or 720p and 30 FPS.

Hotkeys do nothing — another program may use them; pick other keys in Settings → Recording.

Where is my data? — Settings → About & privacy shows the folders. Your videos are never copied or deleted.

live.title: Live Coach (experimental)
live.subtitle: Short tips in the top-left corner while you play, from a few screenshots.
live.warning:
Before you turn it on:
• Use it for practice: Creative, Free Build, Box Fights, Zone Wars with friends. Do NOT use it in Ranked or tournaments: real-time help from third-party tools can break Epic's competitive rules.
• It sees 1 screenshot every 2 seconds and tips arrive about 5–20 seconds later, so it coaches situations and habits (protection, high ground, heals, storm, materials), not sub-second edits. The full analysis after the game is far more precise.
• Each tip is one Gemini request from your Free Tier quota (by default from a separate Flash-Lite model, so video analysis keeps its quota).
• Small FPS cost (screen capture). Fortnite must be in Windowed Fullscreen to see the tips over the game.
• It only looks at the screen like a viewer: no game memory, no input, no automation.

help.search.title: What to search (YouTube · TikTok · Google)
help.search.body:
• For every mistake the AI writes the exact phrase to search for that situation (e.g. “fortnite pre fire double edit box fight”).
• It is shown on each mistake in the report, on each exercise, and in the What to search card on the dashboard, ordered by what you struggle with most (repeated first).
• One click opens the search on YouTube, TikTok or Google, so you always get current tutorials.
help.live.title: Live Coach (experimental)
help.live.body:
• Turn it on once: Settings → Live Coach → read the limits → tick the box → Save. Use Preview the overlay to see where tips appear.
• On the Record card choose Live Coach only or Record video + Live Coach, then Start (or the start hotkey). On/off at any time: {live}.
• Practice only (Creative, Box Fights, Zone Wars). Not in Ranked or tournaments.
• Tips arrive ~5–20 s after the moment and each tip is one free-tier request. Needs Windowed Fullscreen to show over the game.

help.clips.body:
• Clip library finds Medal, NVIDIA, Xbox Game Bar and this app's folders automatically. Add any other folder with Add folder….
• Double-click a clip to open it, or tick up to 10 and click Analyze selected: the app shows the total requests first, then analyzes them one after another.
• Medal folder: Medal → Settings → Recording → Clip folder.
